name: 00 · Cold open
notes:
- **Stage cue — say nothing.** Face the judges, then turn to the Mac camera.
- **Silently mouth:** "How are you doing?" — normal pace, lips clear. Hold ~3 s of silence.
- Turn back. Pause one beat. Then advance and say: **"You just watched me say something. You didn't hear a word."**
- Do NOT pretend to have a disability. You are showing the gap, not playing a patient.

name: 01 · The silence

els.txt: YOU SAW ME SAY SOMETHING. YOU DIDN'T HEAR A WORD.
Losing your voice shouldn't mean losing your place in the conversation.
spans: Losing your voice shouldn't mean losing

notes:
- (0:08) "You just watched me say something. You didn't hear a word."
- "For people who lose their voice — after throat cancer surgery, or with a breathing tube — that's not a trick. It's every conversation."
- **Land the headline. Pause.** Don't read it aloud word for word; let them read it while you breathe.
- Transition: "And here's the thing most people miss —" → next slide.

name: 02 · The human need

els.txt:
The words are still there.
The sound may not be.
“Limited options for speech rehabilitation in the immediate postoperative period, resulting in communication difficulties and patient frustration.”
— Fassler et al., 2026, on the weeks after total laryngectomy ¹
Electrolarynx, voice prosthesis, esophageal speech, writing and AAC all help — each asks for hands, training, healing time or typing speed. ²
of patients after total laryngectomy preferred a lip-reading app to writing things down.
That app is SRAVI — a fixed-phrase research app, not TACIT. 16 patients, 652 uses. Right phrase on the first try 43%, overall 67%. Small and imperfect — and still preferred. ¹
¹ Fassler CA et al. Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 2026;174(2):582–586. PMID 41485241.     ² ASHA Practice Portal: Communication After Total Laryngectomy.

notes:
- (0:20) "Your mind still forms the words. Your lips still shape them. What can be lost is the sound."
- "After a total laryngectomy, people do relearn to speak — electrolarynx, voice prosthesis — and those tools are real and good. But they need hands, training, healing time."
- Point to the card: "In a 2026 clinical study, most patients right after surgery preferred a **lip-reading app** to writing — even at 43% first-try accuracy."
- **Say the caveat yourself:** "That's someone else's app, a fixed phrase list, 16 patients. It tells us people want this — not that we've solved it."
- Transition: "So we asked: what if your lips could speak in any conversation — in your own words?"

name: 03 · Introducing TACIT

els.txt: TACIT turns silent articulation into a way to speak.
You shape the words silently toward your Mac's camera.
Visual speech recognition, running locally. Lips only — no microphone.
Words appear in the notch. Edit, or tap Speak. Nothing is sent before you do.
The approved words are spoken in the voice you chose.
A virtual microphone carries them into Google Meet, Zoom, any call app.
Real captures from the deployed native macOS app. The review step is the safety design: lip reading can be wrong, so you always see the words first.

notes:
- (0:45) "This is TACIT. A native Mac app that lives in the notch."
- Walk left → right, one breath each: "I mouth the words. TACIT reads my lips — on the Mac, no microphone. The words show up in the notch. I fix them or tap Speak. They're spoken in the voice I chose, into the microphone of a normal Google Meet call."
- **Emphasise tile 3:** "That review step is on purpose. Lip reading gets words wrong. So nothing reaches the call until I say so."
- Transition: "Let me show you instead of telling you." → walk to the Mac.

name: 04 · Live demo

els.txt: I mouth “How are you doing?” — silently
TACIT shows exactly what it read
I fix a word if needed, then tap Speak
You hear it from the other side of the call
Backup if the room beats the camera: the same live recognizer on a recorded silent clip — and we'll say it's recorded.
Real capture · Review first — only Speak sends these words

notes:
- (1:10) **Leave this slide up only as a cue.** Stay silent from mouthing until Speak, then press **Pause** before talking (TACIT reads any lip movement). Eyes go to the Mac, not the screen.
- Click the notch → **Start communicating**. Mouth **"How are you doing?"** at the camera.
- Words appear. If exact → "That's what it read. Nothing has been said yet." Tap **Speak**.
- If one word is wrong → **this is the best moment of the pitch**: "It misread one word. That's exactly why I review." Tap **Edit**, fix, **Speak**.
- Judge holds the phone on the Meet call: "You're the other person on this call — tell us what you heard."
- **Only say 'Meet heard it' if the judge actually heard it.**
- Fallback ladder: see TACIT_Live_Demo_Runbook.md (Level 2 recorded clip → Level 3 film excerpt). Always announce recorded input.

name: 05 · What makes it different

els.txt: AI does the reading. You do the deciding.
+ your point, in a few words

see the words
edit anything
tap Speak
macOS voice or your consented clone
AI never edits the words TACIT read from your lips.
Nothing reaches the call until you tap Speak.
Gemini needs your own point before it drafts an opinion.
Queued and playing speech cancelled — 22 ms in our checks.
Real-time (unreviewed) mode exists for practised phrases: off by default, opt-in per session behind an explicit warning, always labelled REAL-TIME.

notes:
- (2:05) "Under the hood: the camera feeds Apple's on-device lip tracking, then an open-source visual speech model running locally on the Mac."
- "Gemini does something different. When typing a reply is too slow, I paste what they said, choose a move — like *share my view* — and type my point in a few words. Gemini turns that into a natural sentence."
- **Point at the mint box:** "Both paths stop here. With me."
- "AI never rewrites what it read from my lips. Gemini can't invent my opinion — it refuses if I haven't given one. And Stop cancels speech in about 20 milliseconds."
- Transition: "So where does that leave us?"

name: 06 · The takeaway

els.txt:
Your words.
Your voice.
Beyond speech.
Silent words → your review → your chosen voice → a call's microphone, on one Mac.
Accuracy across people, faces and rooms. Any testing with people who have lost their voice.
Personal models that don't forget other speakers. Co-design with speech-language pathologists. Real speed and error rates in real calls.

We aren't trying to decide what someone should say.
We're trying to give them another way to be heard.
spans: We aren't trying to decide what someone should say.
We're trying to give them another way to be heard.

notes:
- (2:30) "Today it works end to end on one Mac. It is not proven: lip reading across different people and rooms is still hard, and we haven't tested with people who've lost their voice. That's next — with speech-language pathologists, not around them."
- **Slow down. Final line, look at the judges, not the screen:**
- "We aren't trying to decide what someone should say. We're trying to give them another way to be heard."
- Stop talking. Smile. "Happy to show anything again." (Appendix A1–A8 for questions.)

- Use when asked "how accurate is it?" Lead with the honest number: **73.7% word error on my own held-back silent sentences** with the stock model.

- The 'GOING' row is a real miss — use it to show why the Edit step exists.

name: A2 · What we tried

els.txt: APPENDIX · WHAT WE TRIED, WHAT FAILED
We made it better for one person — and chose not to ship it.
word error rate (lower is better) after fine-tuning on 101 of my silent clips
the same model got worse for everyone else
Our rule, written before the results: other speakers may get at most 1 point worse. It got 3.9 points worse.
Not deployed. The demo runs the unmodified model.

• AirPods jaw-motion sensing — couldn't reliably tell words apart; parked as research.
• Mouthing to pick 1 of 3 AI replies — not the user's own words; replaced by open vocabulary + review.
• Blending back toward the base model — kept only 56% of the gain.
Rules pre-registered 15 Nov 2026 00:30 UTC, before any result · experimental development data, not a guarantee for the deployed model · logs in recognition/data/eval.

notes:
- HackUMass asks what you tried, what failed, what you learned. This is the answer.
- "Fine-tuning on my own silent speech cut my error rate from 74% to 42%. But it got worse for other speakers. We'd written the rule down before seeing results, it failed, so we didn't ship it."
- Lesson: personal adaptation needs more data and rehearsal of other voices — that experiment is running now (prompts recorded separately; not in the demo).

name: A4 · Consent, privacy, control

els.txt: Built so nothing speaks for you.
Lip tracking and recognition run locally. Silent speech never uses your microphone.
Speech needs Live on for this session and your tap on Speak. The exact text is hash-checked: what you saw is what's spoken.
Results from an old utterance, a paused session or an ended call are discarded — never spoken.
Stop and Pause cancel queued and playing audio — 22 ms in our checks.
Gemini sees only what you give it
Text you paste or type, fenced as untrusted. Content is never logged or stored.
Cloning only from your own consented sample. Substituted voices are labelled. Logging is opt-in, off by default.
Enforced in server code (speak_reviewed authorization: Live generation + utterance id + candidate index + text hash) and covered by reviewed:check 13/13.

notes: - Use for privacy / safety questions. Everything here is enforced in code and tested; nothing here is a clinical claim.

name: A5 · Where TACIT fits

els.txt: A handheld device makes the sound
Electronic tone; needs a hand and dexterity ²
Surgical valve; closest to natural voice
No device; air from the esophagus
Long learning period; short, quiet phrases ²
Type, then it's shown or spoken
As fast as you can type
Mouth one phrase from a fixed list
Closed phrase set; phone app; clinical pilots ¹ ³
Mouth any sentence → review → any call

We didn't find this combination elsewhere in our search — that's not a claim to be first.   ¹ Fassler 2026   ² ASHA Practice Portal   ³ Musalia 2023 (14 tracheostomy patients: 75% rank-1, 86% top-3, fixed phrases).

notes:
- "Electrolarynx and voice prostheses are the standard of care and work well for many people. TACIT is an extra path for situations where those don't fit — like the weeks after surgery, or when hands are busy."
- Apple Live Speech: typing → speech in calls. TACIT's difference: no typing — you mouth the sentence.

name: A7 · Before anyone relies on it

els.txt: APPENDIX · BEFORE ANYONE RELIES ON IT
Held-out silent recordings: word error, abstention, wrong-word transmissions, false triggers from non-speech. Today: not validated — so automatic speech stays off by default.
Co-design with the people it's for
People who use alaryngeal speech or AAC, and speech-language pathologists, shape the flow before we add features.
Communication speed, errors and preference versus writing — the questions the SRAVI studies asked.
A model we're allowed to ship
Auto-AVSR's LRS3 weights are research / non-commercial only. A product needs licensed or self-trained weights.
More personal data plus rehearsal of other speakers, judged by the same pre-registered rule.

notes: - For 'what would you need before real users?' and 'is the model commercially usable?' (No — research licence.)
